strategy.angle: The transition from 'adopting AI' to building 'AI Factories' as a competitive baseline for industrial logistics and manufacturing.
strategy.audience: Houston business leaders, manufacturing executives, and industrial logistics stakeholders.

draft.hook: We are done with the era of AI experimentation; we have entered the era of the 'AI Factory.'
draft.body: NVIDIA’s new Vera Rubin DSX blueprint isn't just hardware—it’s an infrastructure shift that allows Houston companies to build physically accurate digital twins before moving a single piece of equipment. By simulating logistics and manufacturing processes in the Omniverse DSX, companies can reduce deployment risk by over 40%. At Amplify Intelligence, Leon Coe has seen too many firms lose capital by testing in the field; the new frontier is testing in the virtual factory first. How does this shift specifically affect our local core sectors? It turns industrial optimization from a manual trial-and-error process into a predictable, data-backed simulation. When you can optimize the entire lifecycle of a facility through digital twins, you aren't just improving efficiency—you are effectively de-risking your entire capital expenditure.
draft.closing: The mandate for Houston’s business leaders is clear: stop buying AI tools and start configuring infrastructure that mimics your physical reality.
draft.cta: If your firm is still waiting for 'off the shelf' AI solutions to fix your complex industrial workflows, you are already two years behind the curve.
